title: حكيمي يفاجئ أوناحي بعد العملية الجراحية

title: بالفيديو.. وائل جمعة يهاجم المغربي بنهاشم: أنت تهدد الأهلي؟

title: Google is cleaning up Home’s messiest bugs, with fixes for cameras, Matter devices, and more
summary: Let's hope this goes a long way towards sorting out some of Google Home's performance issues.
body: TL;DR Google is updating the Home app and Gemini with all its latest smart home fixes. Gemini should no longer complain about misunderstanding commands you never issued. A number of fixes aim to resolve performance problems with cameras in the app. As anyone who has seriously built up a household around Google Home can attest to, the service can feel like it’s constantly in a state of flux. New fixes are arriving all the time, and today Google just shared word of a big wave of updates arriving for the company’s hardware. But that’s just the half of it, and Google’s also telling us about the latest improvements coming to Gemini and the Google Home app. Google published an almost overwhelming Home changelog earlier today, detailing the past couple weeks’ worth of fixes and upgrades. Some of these read a little familiar, like promises for Gemini to understand us better — and here, specifically, Google’s putting a stop to devices blurting out “sorry, I didn’t understand,” in response to nothing at all.

body: أثارت رعاية جمهورية الكونغو الديمقراطية، لنادي برشلونة، جدلًا كبيرًا، منذ الكشف عن تفاصيل الاتفاق. وتنص الصفقة على تحقيق إيرادات تبلغ 44 مليون يورو على مدار 4 مواسم، وقد أدت إلى تقديم شكوى أثارت تساؤلات بشأن الإجراءات المتبعة لإبرام الاتفاق ومصدر الأموال المخصصة لتمويله. وركز مقدمو الشكوى على احتمال تمويل العقد من المال العام، من دون إجراء مناقصة مسبقة أو الحصول على موافقة البرلمان الكونغولي. وذكرت صحيفة سبورت ، أن النيابة العامة فتحت تحقيقًا أوليًا لدراسة الوقائع، إلا أن القضية لم تتقدم في نهاية المطاف عبر المسار القضائي الإسباني. وقررت النيابة العامة، حفظ الشكوى، معتبرة أن الوقائع لم تحدث في إسبانيا، وبالتالي فإنها لا تملك الاختصاص الإقليمي للتحقيق فيها، وفقًا لما كشف عنه ألبرت ليموس عبر إذاعة كادينا سير. وجاء تقديم الشكوى، عقب إعلان برشلونة، شراكته مع حكومة الكونغو الديمقراطية. وعلى الرغم من أن النيابة العامة فتحت في البداية تحقيقًا أوليًا، فإنها قررت في نهاية المطاف عدم مواصلة التحقيق بسبب مسألة الاختصاص الإقليمي. وكان برشلونة قد أعلن في يوليو 2025، عن شراكة مع الحكومة الكونغولية للترويج للدولة الأفريقية من خلال الرياضة والثقافة. ومن بين المقابل الذي نص عليه الاتفاق، وضع شعار "جمهورية الكونغو الديمقراطية ـ قلب أفريقيا" على الجزء الخلفي من قمصان التدريبات الخاصة بالفرق المحترفة…

Named Teghaza 001 after the salt plain in Mali where it was discovered, the meteorite is one of roughly 435 from the Red Planet. In a paper published Thursday in Science, researchers offered an initial characterization of Teghaza 001, providing a rare snapshot of Mars’ ancient crust and formation. What scientists learn from future studies could help answer many questions, including how water and rocks interacted on ancient Mars. body: 2 min read Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater) The Quantum-Enabled Predictive Preclinical NAMs for Toxicity and Safety (QuSAFE) Challenge, a collaboration between the National Institutes of Health (NIH) and NASA, advances quantum-enabled sensing for in vitro NAMs, such as organoids and microphysiological systems (MPS), to improve drug safety while reducing animal use. In vitro NAMs, such as organoids and microphysiological systems (MPS), can generate human-relevant data for drug development and safety evaluation. However, conventional assays and imaging are often noisy, invasive, and not sensitive enough. As a result, weak, early, and low-abundance biological signals can go undetected, and destructive measurements make it hard to monitor dynamic processes over time. Quantum-enabled sensing approaches can offer ultra-high sensitivity, improved signal-to-noise performance, and nanoscale resolution, overcoming detection and measurement limitations that today’s approaches can’t reach. title: Samsung’s open-ear Galaxy Buds On are coming to the US, and we finally know when
summary: US availability starts next week!
body: TL;DR Samsung’s first open-ear earbuds, the Galaxy Buds On, are coming to the US on November 6 for $229. The clip-style earbuds feature sound leakage reduction, up to 9.5 hours of battery life, wireless charging, and Gemini Live support. The Galaxy Buds On lack ANC and Bluetooth multipoint support, and come in just one size and color. After trying an all-new aspect ratio for its foldable earlier this year, Samsung is also betting on a new earbud design. The South Korean company has stuck to familiar earbud designs in the past, but that’s changing now with the Galaxy Buds On. The tech giant launched the new open-ear Galaxy Buds On in Korea yesterday, and even though they aren’t immediately available in the US, the wait for their eventual availability won’t be long. Samsung has confirmed that the Galaxy Buds On will go on sale stateside on November 6, and they’ll cost $229. That’s just a little over a week to wait at this point.

title: Cooling fans are the next big Android phone trend you should avoid
summary: More and more brands want to put a fan-cooled phone in your pocket, but are they worth it?
body: Credit: Robert Triggs / Android Authority While not an entirely new trend, the HONOR Win 2 series and OnePlus Ace 7 are just two in a growing list of Android phones launching with cooling fans onboard. What was previously just the purview of niche flagship gaming phones is quickly making its way to more affordable handsets with broader appeal. In theory, this technology makes a lot of sense. PCs, laptops , and even handheld game consoles all have fans to help keep them cool while powering through intense workloads. So why shouldn’t high-performance smartphones benefit too, especially given that they’re constrained by small form factors that struggle to dissipate heat quickly?

title: Galaxy Ring and these Galaxy Watches will get improved sleep apnea detection
summary: Galaxy Watches and Rings will categorize breathing disturbances into one of three levels.
body: TL;DR Samsung has received clearance from the US and Korean Food and Drug Safety authorities for an advanced sleep apnea function. Galaxy Watches and Galaxy Ring will soon be able to categorize breathing disturbances into one of three levels: mild, occasional, or frequent. The feature will start rolling out in November to users in South Korea. Sleep apnea detection has long been a feature on Samsung’s wearables. Watches as old as the Galaxy Watch 4 have offered sleep apnea detection, and the Galaxy Ring became the first FDA-cleared ring device for sleep apnea detection earlier this year. However, the company is now introducing a new, more advanced function that could prove helpful beyond just detecting signs of sleep apnea. Samsung has announced that it received clearance from both the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the Korean Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) for the advanced sleep apnea feature.
